# Business English — Syria — Arabic glossary

Every Arabic word a learner can see in this course, in one place.

**This file is generated.** Run `node tools/glossary.js` from
`business-sy/app` after changing any data file. `tools/check.js` reads it
back, so a scene that shows an Arabic gloss this file does not list fails
the gate. The glossary cannot drift from the course, because the course is
where it comes from.

Two honest limits on what follows.

The Arabic is Modern Standard Arabic, written to be read rather than
spoken, because that is what a Syrian learner reads in a contract, an
invoice and a tender document. Several of these terms have a different
everyday Levantine form, and where the business usage really is the
borrowed English word, the gloss says so rather than inventing a
replacement.

These glosses were written as part of building the course and have **not**
been reviewed by a native-speaker translator or by a terminologist. They
are a working draft to be checked, not an authority to be cited. Where a
term is contested in Arabic business usage, the English gloss beside it is
the definition the course actually teaches.

Terms: **357**. Sightings across the book: **468**, in 571 scenes.

---
